query: The Bristle Trim {Professor Brask has the class trimming broom tails. "Broom's a creature. Sulky, stupid creature. Groom it, or it grooms you. Into a hedge."|Bristle day again. Brask inspects each broom tail like a hoof, muttering to the brooms more kindly than to you.|Broom trimming. Your school broom recognises you and shivers.} {A hippogriff watches from the paddock, judging.|One broom keeps flicking its twigs at whoever's trimming it.|{season == "winter": The twigs are brittle with frost and snap if you look at them.|The twigs are green and springy, and fight back.}} Trim it twig by twig {You bind every twig and trim the tail to a perfect curve. Brask looks it over. "Adequate. Broom thinks so too." Your fingers are numb, and the hour felt like three.|You trim for an hour, slowly, and your broom flies straighter for it. It's mindless and it isn't; your back aches.|You trim as Brask taught you, twig by twig. The broom purrs, if a broom can purr. Brask says it can. It's still the dullest hour of your week.} Test-fly it untrimmed {You fly it rough and it flies well anyway, the way some ugly ponies do. Brask watches, grunts, and lets you off.|The untrimmed broom bucks once and then settles under you like an old dog. Brask, drily: "Lucky. Don't count on it."|You know your broom's moods now; you fly it shaggy and it goes like a hawk. Brask almost smiles.} {The shaggy tail catches the wind and you go into the hedge, as Brask predicted. She says so, to the hippogriff.|The broom sheds twigs in mid-air and spins you into the paddock. The hippogriff is unimpressed. So is Brask.|It bucks you off at head height. Brask tells the broom it did well, and tells you to get up.}
